:::{#exm-momentum-coefficient}
#### How far back the velocity remembers

Unrolling the recursion, the vector $\vg^{(t-k)}$ enters $\vv^{(t)}$ with factor $\beta^k$, for $k < t$.
These factors add up to at most $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \beta^k = 1 / (1 - \beta)$.
As a rule of thumb, the [velocity](#def-momentum-coefficient) is therefore dominated by the last $1 / (1 - \beta)$ vectors.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

### R

```{r}
#| label: momentum-coefficient-r
#| code-fold: false
beta_mc <- c(0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99)
k_mc <- 10
weight_mc <- beta_mc^k_mc
memory_mc <- 1 / (1 - beta_mc)
weight_rounded_mc <- signif(weight_mc, 2)
rbind(beta = beta_mc, weight = weight_rounded_mc, memory = memory_mc) # nolint: undesirable_function_linter.
```

### Python

```{python}
#| label: momentum-coefficient-python
#| code-fold: false
beta_mc = [0, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99]
k_mc = 10
for b_mc in beta_mc:
    print(b_mc, float(f"{b_mc**k_mc:.2g}"), round(1 / (1 - b_mc)));
```

:::

At $\beta = 0$ the [velocity](#def-momentum-coefficient) is the current vector alone,
and at $\beta = 0.99$ it combines about `r round(memory_mc[4])` vectors.

<!-- no-figure: the example tabulates weights -->

:::
